title: STATE WINNERS
full_story:
The Flora Elks Lodge 1659 is proud to announce the winners of the 2025-2026 Americanism Essay Contest. This year, students were challenged to reflect on the poignant theme: “What Does Service to Your Country Mean to You?”

The essay submitted by Riley Butcher a 5th grader who goes to Full Armor Christian Academy won the state competition.  Riley will receive a $500 award at the Elks State convention in May.

Two Clay City students also did well, Lucas Pruitt, earned Second Place in the 8th grade division.  Lucas’s essay is officially moving on to the State level for judging.  Raeley Rawls also placed in the 6th Grade division.

title: WILHOUR TRAVELING OFFICE HOURS
full_story:
State Representative Blaine Wilhour announced that Traveling Office Hours for constituents to meet with legislative staff to receive help with state programs will be held on Wednesday.   Wilhour’s representatives will be available on Wednesday, from 8:30 AM to 10:00 AM at the Ramsey Village Hall from 10:30 AM to 12:30 PM at the Evans Public Library in Vandalia and from 2:00 PM to 3:30 PM at the Mulberry Grove Village Hall.

On Wednesday April 8th legislative staff will be available at the Case-Halstead Library in Carlyle, from 9:00 am to 10:30 am, at the Centralia Regional Library from 11:00 am to 12:30 pm, and at the Bryan-Bennett Library in Salem from 2:00 pm to 3:30 pm.

Traveling Office Hours will also be held on Wednesday, April 15th at the Olney Public Library from 1 to 3 pm.

Representative Wilhour said “My staff will be available to meet with constituents about public policy issues and concerns as well as provide help with state programs.  I encourage everyone to sign up for my electronic news updates to learn about the activities of the General Assembly and encourage you to take advantage of the online technology to monitor legislative proceedings and file witness slips on legislation that you agree with or disagree with.”

Constituents may contact the district office at 618-665-4109 or online at RepWilhour.com to schedule an appointment to meet with the legislative staff.

title: FMH ANNOUNCES 2 ADDITIONS
full_story:
Fairfield Memorial Hospital is pleased to announce that Connie Henshaw, Advanced Practice Nurse(APN), Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP), has joined the organization as a Hospitalist, providing care to patients in the Med/Surg ICU Department.  Also, Samantha Sisco, Advanced Practice Nurse (APN), Family Nurse Practitioner-Certified (FNP-C), Wound Care Certified (WCC), has joined the organization and will lead its Wound Care Clinic.

Henshaw is an American Association of Nurse Practitioners (AANP) board-certified Family Nurse Practitioner with a strong background in acute care, critical care, and emergency nursing.  In her new role, she will deliver comprehensive inpatient care, working collaboratively with physicians, nurses, and interdisciplinary teams to ensure high-quality outcomes for patients with complex medical needs.

Fairfield Memorial Hospital’s Hospitalist Program is dedicated to providing continuous, coordinated care for hospitalized patients, ensuring safety, efficiency, and improved patient outcomes.

Sisco is a Board Certified National Alliance of Wound Care and Ostomy (NAWCO) Clinician (WCC), demonstrating advanced expertise in wound management and a strong commitment to delivering evidence-based care.  In her new role, she will oversee the hospital’s Wound Care Clinic, providing comprehensive evaluation, treatment, and management of acute and chronic wounds.

The Wound Care Clinic at Fairfield Memorial Hospital offers specialized care for patients with non-healing wounds, utilizing advanced treatments and a multidisciplinary approach to promote healing and improve outcomes.

For more information about services at Fairfield Memorial Hospital, please call 618-842-2611.

title: GUILTY OF MURDER
full_story:
A Jefferson County man was found guilty in the death of his wife.

The verdict came down on Friday after three hours of deliberation.  52-year-old John Finney was convicted on multiple counts of murder.

Prosecutors say Amy Jo Finney was found shot inside a vehicle Finney was driving after a traffic stop in September of 2025.  Investigators believe she was killed a day earlier inside her home.

The trial lasted several days.  The defense called no witnesses and Finney did not testify.

title: TEXT MESSAGE SCAMS
full_story:
Attorney General Kwame Raoul is urging Illinois consumers to be alert for scam text messages claiming they committed a traffic or tollway violation and must pay a fine.  Raoul’s office is warning that the unsolicited text messages are intended to trick consumers into sharing personal and financial information.

“Illinois residents should be assured that government agencies will not call, text or email unprompted to ask for payment or personal information,” Raoul said.  “If you receive such a message, even if the phone number appears to be local, do not respond.  If you are unsure if the request is legitimate, contact the agency through the information provided on its official website.”

The Attorney General’s office cautions residents against assuming a text is legitimate because it is sent from a familiar phone number, area code or contains a letter that may look official.  Raoul explained scammers use caller ID to spoof phone numbers to make it appear as though the text is from a reliable source in an effort to convince recipients to provide personal information, click links that will install malware on devices, or click on a web link to a spoofed website.  If recipients attempt to enter usernames and passwords to access these fake websites, scammers may have the ability to access or steal personal information.

Attorney General Raoul encourages consumers who think they have been the victim of identity theft or other fraud to file a complaint on the Attorney General’s website or with the Federal Bureau of Investigations’ (FBI) Internet Crime Complaint Center.  People can review the identity theft resources on Raoul’s website and call Raoul’s toll-free Identity Theft Hotline at 866-999-5630.

title: 911 UPDATE
full_story:
The Illinois State Police (ISP) announced all 169 Public Safety Answering Points (PSAPs) throughout Illinois, commonly called 911 call centers, have successfully transitioned to Next Generation 911 (NG911).  NG911 upgrades the traditional 911 service from voice-centric networks to secure, IP-based infrastructure designed to support today’s communications.

“This milestone reflects years of coordinated work by the ISP Division of Statewide 911, PSAPs, Emergency Telephone System Boards (ETSBs), local and regional stakeholders, and public and private partners,” said ISP Director Brendan F. Kelly.  “Illinois has moved into the 21st century for 911 communication offering more efficient emergency services.”

Transitions to NG911 began with the first PSAP switching from the old to the new system in Grundy County on June 21st, 2022, and concluded with the final PSAP cutover to AT&T Statewide ESInet in Northbrook on March 4th.

The upgrade to NG911 means people in Illinois will have more efficient and reliable 911 emergency services.  In a legacy 911 system, a wireless call to 911 could be routed to emergency services based on the location of a cell tower as opposed to the location of the caller.  That could mean the call would have to be transferred to emergency services that were closer to the caller, causing a delay in response time.  NG911 improves this by supporting geospatial call routing based on the caller’s actual location.  NG911 also provides redundant capabilities for reliable service.  For example, if multiple PSAPs were unable to operate in southern Illinois due to damaging storms and tornadoes, emergency calls in that area could be rerouted automatically and handled by PSAPs in other parts of the state.

Additionally, NG911 supports the continued expansion and reliability of Text-to-911, helping ensure equitable access to emergency services for individuals who cannot place a voice call.  The upgraded system allows for more flexibility as 911 services evolve, including the potential to eventually allow for photo and video sharing between residents and PSAPs during emergency situations.
